title: The Last Lit House
description: At eight forty the whole grid went dark, except one house on Pell Court that's now blazing brighter than ever and somehow pulling the entire city's power into itself. Ronnie gets the three people who could cut it on one line, and every one of them swears the surplus is metered to somebody else's address. Meanwhile the homeowner narrates his appliances waking up live.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and folks, the whole town just went dark at eight forty. Except one house. One house on Pell Court, lit up like the sun, somehow pulling the entire grid into itself. Tonight we've got the three people who can throw the breaker, all on one line. Patricia from the Power Authority, Winston from the city, and Marco with the line crew. Welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: One quick thing before we start. Can somebody just pull the meter?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We'll get to the meter, Barry. Now that's free heat for the whole street, if you think about it. Patricia, you're closest to this. What are we looking at?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Well, Ronnie, I've pulled the load chart, and I want to be very clear. <p:0.3> That draw on Pell Court isn't on our side of the pole. Per the load chart, all that surplus is being delivered to a meter two streets over. So whatever's lighting up that house, it isn't ours to cut.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Patricia, it's going to a different meter. <p:0.3> The house is on fire with electricity and it's somebody else's bill.

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: Uh, hi, Ronnie. It's Edwin, inside the house. <p:0.3> My porch light just came on. I never turned it on. It's reading forty watts. Over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Thanks for the update, Edwin, hang in there. Winston, the city's grid assets, that's your wheelhouse.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It is precisely NOT my wheelhouse, Ronnie. I handle assets at rest. Substations, transformers, things that sit still. <p:0.3> Electricity is moving. A current in motion is a different asset class entirely. Not mine.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, but Marco, your crew cut that line tonight. Right?

lines.speaker: caller-marco
lines.text: We de-energized it, Barry. I watched it go dead with my own eyes. <p:0.3> So whatever's feeding that house, I'll tell you right now, that's not the line we cut.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's... that's not the line you cut. But you cut a line.

lines.speaker: caller-marco
lines.text: We cut a different line, Barry. A dead one. The hot one, the one doing all this? Different line entirely. Not the one we cut.

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: [surprise-oh] Update, Ronnie. The microwave came back on. <p:0.3> It's been unplugged since March. It's asking me things now. Eleven hundred watts. Over.

lines.speaker: meter-vox
lines.text: Great news! Your household usage is up four thousand percent. You've been automatically upgraded to our Platinum Surplus tier. No action needed. Have a luminous evening!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who said that? Ronnie, who is upgrading him? Nobody touch the upgrade, just pull the meter!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: That's not our meter talking, Barry. Per the load chart, that draw isn't on our side of the pole. You can't bill from a pole that isn't ours.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's fair. Marco, if Patricia's pole is clean and Winston's assets are at rest, then the hot line must be the one your crew was on.

lines.speaker: caller-marco
lines.text: On is not the same as cut, Ronnie. We were on a lot of lines tonight. The one that's glowing, I keep telling you, that's not the one we cut.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: And it's flowing, which makes it a live load, which makes it not mine. I catalogue assets at rest. A glowing house is somebody else's category.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It is getting BRIGHTER, Winston! A man's appliances are waking up!

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: Update. The fridge I unplugged in March is humming a tune. <p:0.3> It's the one from the radio. It knows the words. Six hundred watts. Over.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Just pull the meter! Somebody! PULL THE METER!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Not our pole!

lines.speaker: caller-marco
lines.text: Different line!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Asset class!

lines.speaker: meter-vox
lines.text: GREAT NEWS!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: PULL THE METER!

lines.speaker: meter-vox
lines.text: Great news! Your meter has been upgraded to read-only. <p:0.3> There is no longer an off. Enjoy the glow!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Edwin? <p:0.3> Edwin, you still with us?

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: ...Edwin's resting now. <p:0.4> The house has the line. Twelve thousand watts. <p:0.3> And climbing. Over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, folks, by unanimous agreement, that surplus belongs to nobody at all. <p:0.3> So congratulations to Pell Court, the brightest house in the county. Wave if you see Edwin's porch light. We'll be right back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. <p:0.3> I can see his porch light from the studio. Through the wall.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's fair. <p:0.3> Was that on a minute ago?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It wasn't, Ronnie. <p:0.3> And our lights just got brighter.
